en: vt. to mix two or more substances together; to combine different things so that they form a new whole; vi. to mix well together; to look similar to what is around; n. a mixture of different things
ex: Blend the eggs and sugar until smooth.
把蛋和糖攪拌至滑順。

en: vi. to open and close your eyes quickly; (of a light) to shine on and off; vt. to close and open your eyes quickly; n. a very short moment; a quick opening and closing of the eyes
ex: She blinked in the bright sunlight.
她在刺眼的陽光下眨了眨眼。
ph: in the blink of an eye

en: n. a statement in which you say that you are very good at something; something that you are proud of; vi. to talk too proudly about what you have done; vt. to be proud to possess something
ex: He likes to boast about his new car.
他喜歡吹噓自己的新車。

en: vi. to jump up and down; (of a ball) to hit a surface and come back; to move in a lively way; vt. to make something bounce; n. a jump; the ability to bounce; energy
ex: The ball bounced off the wall.
球從牆上彈了回來。

en: n. a man who is about to be married or has just been married; the male partner in a wedding
ex: The bridegroom waited at the altar with a smile.
新郎帶著微笑在祭壇前等待。

en: n. a brush with a long handle used for sweeping floors; a shrub with yellow flowers; vt. to sweep with a broom
ex: She swept the kitchen floor with a broom.
她用掃帚掃廚房的地板。

en: a. cruel and showing no kindness or pity; very direct and honest in a way that may upset people; extremely severe or bad
ex: The dictator was known for his brutal treatment of prisoners.
那位獨裁者以殘酷對待囚犯聞名。

en: n. a short official statement or news report; a printed notice issued regularly by an organization
ex: The school posted a bulletin about the field trip.
學校貼出關於校外教學的公告。

en: n. a piece of furniture with shelves or drawers for storing things; a group of senior ministers who advise the head of a government; a. (of furniture) made by a skilled carpenter; relating to the cabinet in government
ex: The plates are in the kitchen cabinet.
盤子放在廚房櫥櫃裡。

en: n. the process of using mathematics to find an amount; a careful consideration of something before making a decision; the result of calculating something
ex: The calculation shows that we need fifty more chairs.
計算結果顯示我們還需要五十張椅子。

en: n. a long thin stick used to support someone when walking; the long thin stem of some plants; a stick used to hit someone as a punishment; vt. to hit someone with a cane; to make furniture from cane
ex: The old man walked slowly with the help of a cane.
老人拄著拐杖慢慢走。

en: n. a light narrow boat that you move through the water with a paddle; vi. to travel in a canoe; vt. to carry something by canoe
ex: They paddled a canoe down the river.
他們划著獨木舟順河而下。

en: n. the amount of space that something has for holding things; the ability to do something; the position or role of a person; the maximum amount that can be produced
ex: The stadium has a capacity of fifty thousand people.
這座體育場可容納五萬人。

en: n. a person who owns a lot of money or a business and uses it to make more money; a person who supports capitalism; a. relating to capitalism
ex: The capitalist invested heavily in new technology.
資本家對新科技大量投資。

en: n. a complete list of items, such as the products you can buy from a company; a book with a list of courses at a school; vt. to make a list of things in a particular order
ex: I looked through the catalogue to find a new sofa.
我翻閱型錄找新沙發。

en: n. a group of things or people that have similar characteristics; a division in a system of classification
ex: Books are arranged by category on the shelves.
書本依類別排在書架上。

en: n. a party or special event held to show that you are happy about something; the act of celebrating something; a special event to mark an important occasion
ex: The whole town joined in the New Year celebration.
全鎮的人都參加了新年慶祝活動。

en: n. an organization that gives money or help to people in need; the act of giving money to people in need; kindness and generosity towards others; (in the Bible) love for other people
ex: She raised money for a children's charity.
她為一個兒童慈善機構募款。

en: vt. to stop someone from breathing by squeezing their throat or blocking their air passage; to block a pipe or passage; vi. to be unable to breathe; to be unable to speak because of emotion; n. a device that controls the amount of air entering an engine
ex: He choked on a piece of meat and could not breathe.
他被一塊肉噎住，無法呼吸。

en: n. a group of people who sing together; a part of a song that is repeated; a number of people or things saying or doing something at the same time; v. to sing or speak together
ex: The church chorus sang beautifully on Sunday.
教會合唱團在週日唱得非常優美。

en: a. shaped like a circle; moving in a circle and returning to the start; (of a letter or advertisement) sent to many people; (of an argument) not logical because the conclusion is the same as the premise
ex: The table is circular and seats six people.
這張桌子是圓形的，可坐六個人。

en: n. the movement of liquid or air around a closed system, such as blood in the body; the movement of something from one person to another; the number of copies of a newspaper or magazine that are sold
ex: Regular exercise improves blood circulation.
規律運動能促進血液循環。

en: n. a fight or disagreement between people or groups; a loud noise made when metal objects hit each other; a situation in which two events happen at the same time and conflict; vi. to fight or disagree; vt. to make a loud noise by hitting things together
ex: There was a clash between the police and the protesters.
警方與抗議者發生衝突。

en: n. the act of putting people or things into groups according to their characteristics; a system of grouping things; a group into which something is placed
ex: The classification of plants helps scientists study them.
植物的分類幫助科學家研究它們。

en: vt. to put people or things into groups according to their characteristics; to officially declare information as secret; to arrange something in a system
ex: Libraries classify books by subject.
圖書館依主題將書籍分類。

en: a. moving or doing things in a careless and awkward way; badly made or difficult to use; (of a remark or action) showing a lack of tact
ex: He is so clumsy that he often drops things.
他笨手笨腳，常常把東西掉到地上。

en: a. rough and not smooth to touch; (of language or behavior) rude and offensive; made of large pieces, not fine ones
ex: The fabric was too coarse for a baby's skin.
這塊布料對嬰兒的皮膚來說太粗糙了。

en: n. a system of words, letters or symbols used to send secret messages; a set of rules that people must follow; the instructions of a computer program; vt. to put a message into a secret code
ex: The spy sent a message in code.
間諜以密碼傳送訊息。

en: n. a funny play, film or television show; funny entertainment in general; a funny or amusing situation
ex: We watched a romantic comedy last night.
我們昨晚看了一部愛情喜劇。

en: n. the activity of buying and selling goods on a large scale; business activity between countries or companies
ex: The city is a center of international commerce.
這座城市是國際商業中心。

en: n. the activity of sharing information with others by speaking, writing or using other methods; a message; a way of sending information; a means of traveling between places
ex: Good communication is the key to a happy marriage.
良好的溝通是幸福婚姻的關鍵。

en: n. an event in which people try to win by being better than others; the activity of trying to win something; the people who are trying to win; a situation in which people compete for something
ex: She won first prize in the singing competition.
她在歌唱比賽中贏得第一名。

en: a. involving competition; wanting to be more successful than others; (of a price) as low as or lower than others
ex: The company offers competitive salaries to attract talent.
公司提供有競爭力的薪資來吸引人才。

en: vt. to form something by putting parts together; to write a piece of music or a poem; to make yourself calm; vi. to write music or poetry
ex: She composed a beautiful song for her mother.
她為母親寫了一首美麗的歌。

en: n. a short piece of writing, especially one done at school; a piece of music or art; the way in which something is formed from different parts; the parts that something is made of
ex: The teacher asked us to write a composition about our summer holiday.
老師要我們寫一篇關於暑假的作文。

en: v. to give all your attention to something; to bring things together in one place; to make a liquid stronger by removing water; n. a liquid made by removing water from something
ex: I find it hard to concentrate with so much noise.
吵成這樣我很難專心。

en: prep. about or relating to something; connected with a subject; (as part of a participle) worrying someone
ex: I need some information concerning the new rules.
我需要一些有關新規定的資訊。

en: n. a large formal meeting where people discuss ideas, often lasting several days; a meeting of a group of people to discuss something; an association of sports teams
ex: She is presenting a paper at an international conference next week.
她下週將在國際會議上發表論文。

en: v. to admit that you have done something wrong; to tell a priest about your sins; to admit that you do not know or cannot do something; to tell the truth
ex: He confessed that he had broken the window.
他坦承是他打破了窗戶。

en: vt. to tell someone that you are pleased about their success or good luck; to praise someone for something they have achieved
ex: I'd like to congratulate you on your promotion.
我想恭喜你升職。
